page: Amazon Web Services m7g.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton3 processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores built on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The processor lacks hyperthreading, providing exactly one thread per core. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7g.metal demonstrates strong multi-threaded and memory performance. Its Geekbench multi-core score of 20845.0 and software compilation score of 60170.0 both rank in the top tier, representing the top 10% of tested systems. The Passmark memory score of 3172.17 also places in the top tier, reflecting the high bandwidth of DDR5 memory. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1537.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 34677.75, both falling in the average range. The server also shows strong capabilities in physics simulations and database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the arm64 architecture and dedicated bare-metal resources offer high compute density and predictable performance without hyperthreading overhead. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, requiring external network-attached storage. This server is recommended for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, containerized microservices, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory bandwidth.
